title: Isandro and the Tide
premise: Wendell Vane, a wedding planner who stopped believing in weddings after their own collapsed, finds a letter lost in the mail for eleven years — written by Isandro Reyes, the person they loved and abandoned, confessing he had waited for them at a train station that never saw them arrive. Wendell tracks Isandro to a fading coastal town where he now runs his late mother's tide-pool aquarium, unaware of what the letter will reopen. As Wendell stays to help save the aquarium from demolition, old love and old guilt collide, forcing them to finally speak the apology rehearsed for a decade. In the end, on the beach where the letter was meant to be answered, Wendell says it aloud — and chooses, this time, to stay.
about_author: Marguerite Almeida is the pen name of a former archivist who spent years cataloguing other people's letters before writing her own stories about them. She lives near the Atlantic coast, where she collects unsent mail and insists every tide brings something back.

chapters.title: The Unsent Archive
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. Three years into rebuilding their life through flawless, feelingless weddings, Wendell sorts a deceased client's estate and finds an envelope postmarked eleven years ago, addressed to them in handwriting they'd know anywhere. The beat: dread disguised as curiosity, the safe life cracking at its first seam.

chapters.title: Eleven Years of Weather
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. They read the letter in fragments across a sleepless night: Isandro waited at the station; Wendell never came. Flashbacks braid the past collapse with the present. The beat: grief resurfacing, and the terrible realization the letter demands an answer a decade late.

chapters.title: Postmark: Salt Hollow
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. A return address leads to Salt Hollow, a shrinking coastal town. Wendell tells themselves they're only returning the letter, booking one week off between weddings. The beat: denial as momentum, packing a bag like an escape route.

chapters.title: The Man at the Aquarium
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. Isandro repairs the tide-pool tanks of his late mother's aquarium, dodging the developer's demolition notices, when a familiar figure appears at the gate holding an envelope older than his grief. The beat: shock held very still, like touching a sea urchin.

chapters.title: What the Letter Said
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. They finally sit face to face; Isandro reads his own eleven-year-old words aloud, voice breaking on the last line. He is not the boy who waited anymore, and says so. The beat: humiliation and tenderness tangled, no absolution offered yet.

chapters.title: One Week Becomes Two
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. Their rental car breaks down; the town has one mechanic and slow parts. Stuck, Wendell volunteers at the aquarium's failing summer fundraiser, telling themselves it's practical. The beat: the first unguarded laugh in three years, immediately distrusted.

chapters.title: Tide Charts
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. Isandro teaches Wendell the tide pools — when to look, when the water hides everything. Old intimacy flickers in shared competence. But a demolition hearing notice arrives, dated two weeks out. The beat: warmth shadowed by a ticking clock.

chapters.title: The Wedding Planner Plans Nothing
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. Back home, clients email demanding attention; Wendell drafts replies and deletes them. A rival planner circles their biggest account. The beat: the safe life revealed as a cage they built themselves, measured in small safe steps going nowhere.

chapters.title: His Mother's Tanks
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. Isandro shows Wendell the archive room: his mother's research, her own unsent letters, her belief that nothing living should be left behind. Wendell recognizes the shape of inherited guilt. The beat: mutual recognition — both are curators of things unfinished.

chapters.title: Rehearsal
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. Alone on the breakwater, Wendell rehearses the apology aloud for the first time, the sentence they've carried a decade: why they never came. We learn the truth — fear, not betrayal, kept them from the station. The beat: confession practiced on gulls, still too afraid of its audience.

chapters.title: Storm Season
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. A storm floods the aquarium's lower hall; they work all night hauling tanks and mopping, soaked and laughing and nearly kissing before Isandro pulls back — 'Not until you say it.' The beat: desire and demand colliding, the stakes made explicit.

chapters.title: The Developer's Offer
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. The developer offers Isandro a settlement generous enough to erase his debts — if he stops fighting. Tempted, exhausted, he almost signs. Wendell, seeing the papers, offers to plan a fundraiser gala, the one thing they're brilliant at. The beat: pride versus survival, and Wendell betting their old skill on a new hope.

chapters.title: Gala Preparations
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. Wendell throws themselves into planning the Save the Tide gala — flowers, permits, a band — discovering that planning a cause feels different from planning a performance. Small-town volunteers rally. The beat: vocation redeemed, belonging arriving sideways.

chapters.title: An Old Account Calls
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. The rival planner poaches Wendell's flagship wedding; back home there is nothing left to return to but the office and its silence. Wendell realizes they aren't stranded in Salt Hollow — they're choosing it. The beat: loss reframed as permission.

chapters.title: What Isandro Never Sent
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. Isandro admits he wrote more letters over the years and burned them; the found letter was the last one he ever risked. His anger softens into something more dangerous — wanting. The beat: vulnerability exchanged for vulnerability, the wall coming down brick by brick.

chapters.title: The Night Before the Gala
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Decorations up, tide charts checked, they walk the dark beach and nearly cross the line again. This time Wendell stops themself: 'Tomorrow. Let me do this in order.' The beat: restraint as devotion, tension coiled to snapping.

chapters.title: Save the Tide
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. The gala succeeds beyond hope — donations pour in, the hearing committee wavers — but mid-celebration Wendell freezes at the podium, the old stage fright wearing the old fear's face. Isandro takes their hand in front of everyone. The beat: public triumph inseparable from private terror.

chapters.title: The Sentence
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. After the crowd thins, on the empty beach, Wendell finally says the rehearsed sentence — the whole truth of why they never came to the station. No music, no lighting design, nowhere to hide. The beat: climax; a decade of rehearsal spent in ninety seconds of raw speech.

chapters.title: Low Tide
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. Isandro answers not with instant forgiveness but with honesty: he can't unread eleven years, but he can choose the next eleven. They agree to begin slowly, without guarantees. The beat: aftermath of climax, forgiveness as a decision rather than a feeling.

chapters.title: The Hearing
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. At the demolition hearing, the community testifies; the aquarium wins landmark protection, and the developer withdraws. Isandro asks Wendell, plainly, to stay — not as penance, but as a life. The beat: external resolution mirroring internal choice.

chapters.title: A Wedding, Believed In
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. Months later, Wendell plans one final wedding — a small couple with no budget and enormous love — and finds, to their astonishment, that they believe in it again. Isandro helps fold programs in the aquarium's archive room. The beat: vocation and love reconciled, the theme of inheritance fulfilled.

chapters.title: What the Tide Returns
chapters.summary: Alternating POV closing on Wendell. On the anniversary of the lost letter, they walk to the station platform in Salt Hollow's sister town — the one Isandro waited at — and leave a new letter there, addressed to the boy who waited, signed by the person who finally came. Then they walk home together. The beat: memory honored, belonging chosen, the tide going out and coming back.
